title: Ensure 'Enforce password history' is set to '24 or more password(s)'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to 24 or more password(s): Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Enforce password history [1]
reason: The longer a password is reused, the greater the chance that a threat actor can determine the password through brute force attacks. [2]

title: Ensure 'Maximum password age' is set to '365 or fewer days, but not 0'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to 365 or fewer days, but not 0: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Maximum password age [3]
reason: The longer a password exists the higher the likelihood that it will be compromised by a brute force attack, a threat actor gaining general knowledge about the user, or by the user sharing the password. [4]

title: Ensure 'Minimum password age' is set to '1 or more day(s)'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to 1 or more day(s): Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password age [5]
reason: Users may have favorite passwords that they like to use because they are easy to remember Unfortunately, passwords are compromised and if a threat actor is targeting a specific individual's user account, with foreknowledge of data about that user, reuse of old passwords can cause a security breach. [6]

title: Ensure 'Minimum password length' is set to '14 or more character(s)'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to 14 or more character(s): Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password length [7]
reason: Types of password attacks include dictionary attacks (which attempt to use common words and phrases) and brute force attacks (which try every possible combination of characters). [8]

title: Ensure 'Password must meet complexity requirements' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to Enabled: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Password must meet complexity requirements [9]
reason: Passwords that contain only alphanumeric characters are extremely easy to discover with several publicly available tools. [10]

title: Ensure 'Relax minimum password length limits' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to Enabled: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Relax minimum password length limits [11, 12]
reason: This setting will enable the enforcement of longer and generally stronger passwords or passphrases where MFA is not in use. [13]

title: Ensure 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' is set to 'Disabled'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to Disabled: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Store passwords using reversible encryption [14]
reason: Enabling this policy setting allows the operating system to store passwords in a weaker format that is much more susceptible to compromise and weakens your system security. [15]

title: Ensure 'Account lockout duration' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to 15 or more minute(s): Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Account lockout duration [16]
reason: A denial-of-service (DoS) condition can be created if a threat actor abuses the Account lockout threshold and repeatedly attempts to log on with a specific account. [17]

title: Ensure 'Account lockout threshold' is set to '5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s), but not 0'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to 5 or fewer invalid login attempt(s), but not 0: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Account lockout threshold [18]
reason: Setting an account lockout threshold reduces the likelihood that an online password brute force attack will be successful. [19]

title: Ensure 'Allow Administrator account lockout' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to Enabled: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policies\Allow Administrator account lockout [20]
reason: Enabling account lockout policies for the built-in Administrator account will reduce the likelihood of a successful brute force attack. [21]

title: Ensure 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
remediation: To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to 15 or more minute(s): Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Reset account lockout counter after [22]
reason: If the account lockout policy is left at its default setting or configured with an excessively long interval, the environment may be vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. [23]
